purpose: Canonical schema and taxonomy for the general gym strength-and-conditioning exercise library. Draft research files must map into this shape before Mongo ingestion.

record_schema.name: Human-readable canonical exercise name
record_schema.base_exercise: Canonical family such as Squat, Deadlift, Bench Press, Row, Carry, Pallof Press
record_schema.tier: primary | variation | accessory | machine | regression | progression
record_schema.category: strength | hypertrophy | power | accessory | mobility_activation | conditioning

classification_rules.primary: Broadly useful, common S&C exercise that can appear in normal generated workouts for the right user.
classification_rules.variation: A meaningful version of a base exercise used for specific equipment, loading, stance, range, tempo, or skill reasons.
classification_rules.accessory: Usually selected to support a primary pattern, sport demand, weak link, hypertrophy, tissue capacity, or injury-sensitive goal.
classification_rules.machine: Machine-based option useful for beginners, isolation, substitutions, hypertrophy, or injury-sensitive loading.
classification_rules.regression: Easier or safer version that helps the user learn or return to a pattern.
classification_rules.progression: Harder version requiring more load, stability, mobility, or skill.

difficulty_rules.beginner: Low technical complexity, predictable range, easy to coach, safe with light loads or machine/bodyweight support.
difficulty_rules.intermediate: Requires stable technique, more load, free weights, unilateral control, or bracing under fatigue.
difficulty_rules.advanced: High coordination, high load, high mobility/stability demand, high fatigue cost, or narrow sport/performance context.

merge_rules: Do not keep both singular/plural equipment duplicates unless they are mechanically different.
Do not make every grip or stance a separate primary record. Use variations only when the programming reason is different.
Keep machine alternatives because they matter for beginners, substitutions, hypertrophy, and injury-sensitive plans.
Keep clear regressions and progressions so future blocks can upgrade workouts without inventing new exercises.
Do not copy long source text. Store short paraphrased summaries, cues, and source references.
Every final exercise must have at least one pattern, one quality, one use_when item, one avoid_when item, and one source_ref.
